clue.text: Type showing impudence?

definitions.meaning: in printing, a heavy black typeface used for emphasis
a brazen, cheeky expression

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a certain kind of person is just being cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a heavy printing typeface, and the brazen look of a cheeky, shameless person.

clue.text: Another needless cut

indicators.note: another version of the word needless means its letters are rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: Yet another unnecessary reduction in spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut, as a past participle, means reduced or diminished, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Given protection, being cautious

definitions.meaning: watched over and kept safe, as by a sentry
careful and reserved in what one says

explanation.surface: Someone who is protected and also wary.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a guarded building is protected, and a guarded reply is cautious.

clue.text: Violin part played by a quartet

definitions.meaning: the small upright piece holding the strings off the body of the instrument
the card game for four players in two partnerships

explanation.surface: A section of string music performed by a string quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised wooden support on a violin carries this name, and so does the four-player card game.

clue.text: Information a girl found in Switzerland

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details about a young woman discovered in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on Lake Leman is one of the major places found in Switzerland, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Very nearly put in stifling billet

parts.note: close weather is stifling, airless and humid
a billet is soldiers' lodging, their quarters

explanation.surface: Troops are almost crammed into a stuffy lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very nearly' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition, used adverbially as in 'at very short range'; 'put in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes being very near, as in fighting hand to hand at short range.

clue.text: I, for one!

parts.note: reads as someone volunteering, but the personal pronoun in English is always written as an upper-case character

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly volunteering themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun I is always printed in upper case, making it an example of this kind of character.

clue.text: Behave unexpectedly and quit the chorus?

definitions.meaning: to break the rules or act out of turn
literally, to leave the row of dancers in a chorus line

explanation.surface: A performer misbehaves and walks out of the chorus line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to misbehave or break convention; literally it is stepping out of a row of dancers.

clue.text: Passed shuffled cards

indicators.note: shuffled, like a deck of cards, means the letters of the word passed are mixed up

explanation.surface: A card player passes after the deck has been shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are one of the four suits, so the word names a set of playing cards.

clue.text: Bought back, having had second thoughts?

definitions.meaning: repurchased, as an item from a pawnbroker
read as ..., judged again

explanation.surface: Someone recovered something after reconsidering.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeeming a pawned item means buying it back; split as re-deemed it means judged afresh.

clue.text: Stop a boundary

definitions.meaning: to finish or bring to a halt
a limit or extremity

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt at a border line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to finish and the furthest limit or edge of something.

clue.text: Rain on the way leads to stress and.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Rain on the way leads to stress and.' and ends on a dangling 'and.', so it appears cut short; ST + RAIN = STRAIN with 'stress' as definition fits, but the rest of the clue is missing and a search found no other copy
annotationWithheld.clue: Rain on the way leads to stress and.

clue.text: Resort to a lever for lift

indicators.note: re-sort, sort again, means the letters of to a lever are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone falls back on a crowbar to raise something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as 'turn to', but split as re-sort it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a lift is called by this name, so the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Compete with life in Paris

definitions.meaning: to contend or strive
the French word for life

explanation.surface: Struggling to keep up with Parisian living.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete, and the same spelling is the French noun meaning life.

clue.text: Everyone's prepared, we hear, by the time in question

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: everyone is all, and prepared is ready

explanation.surface: Everyone is apparently set to go at the appointed moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means before or by the time being spoken about, as in 'she had gone by then'.

clue.text: Suffer from partial failure

indicators.note: partial means only part of the word failure is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is afflicted by a partial breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unwell or in trouble is a common sense of suffer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A witty soul, it's said

parts.note: alludes to Polonius's line in Hamlet that a certain quality is the soul of wit

explanation.surface: Someone is reputed to be a clever, amusing person.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Polonius says the quality of saying things in few words is 'the soul of wit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortness in speech is proverbially, from Hamlet, the very soul of wit.

clue.text: Being unable to settle, get up earlier

definitions.meaning: fidgety, unable to stay still
read as ..., take less sleep

explanation.surface: An insomniac rises early because they cannot settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fidgety; split into two words it describes sleeping less by rising earlier.

clue.text: Girl gets a tumultuous hand from the gallery

indicators.note: tumultuous means disordered, so the letters of hand are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer gets loud applause from the upper seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the gallery' suggests applause from the upper seats in a theatre, but the gallery is the definition: a roofed outdoor platform along a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can be a roofed open platform along the outside of a house, the same thing as a porch.

clue.text: Why late changes result in having lots of money

indicators.note: changes means the letters of why late are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking why late alterations lead to riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich and prosperous, a direct synonym for having lots of money.

clue.text: See penal reform in Asian kingdom

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing what is found in the Himalayan country

indicators.note: reform means the letters of see penal are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Observe changes to the penal system in a Himalayan state.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or things from the Himalayan kingdom, which is in Asia.

clue.text: A loose member of the family

parts.note: to loose, as a verb, is to untie or unfasten

explanation.surface: A relative who is a bit wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' reads as an adjective (a loose relation) but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar word for a parent's sister, so a member of the family.

clue.text: Breaking code, he made a resounding comeback

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of code and he are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A cryptographer triumphantly returned after cracking a cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that resounded back off a surface did this, so the phrase defines it wittily.

clue.text: Flying force possibly set out to attack

indicators.note: set out reads as departing, but out signals that these letters are put out of order

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is an example of a flying force, hence possibly

explanation.surface: An air force might set off on an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying force possibly' gives RAF (the Royal Air Force, one example of an air force); 'out' mixes RAF with SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft, a specific kind of attack.

clue.text: Painting skill

definitions.meaning: painting is one form of the visual ...
a craft or knack, as in the ... of conversation

explanation.surface: A talent for painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers the fine arts such as painting, and also craft or knack.

clue.text: Way to stop Henry becoming a writer

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A method to block Henry from becoming an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Marie-Henri Beyle, the French novelist who wrote The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Fast, the Italian's pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: An Italian's heartbeat is racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' reads as a heartbeat but means an edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the edible seed of a leguminous plant, and this small lens-shaped seed is one example.

clue.text: To take up the post is to increase the risk

definitions.meaning: literally, to lift a wooden stake or post
to raise the amount wagered, upping what is at hazard

explanation.surface: Accepting the new job means taking a bigger gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally lifting a wooden post, and figuratively upping the wager, so increasing what could be lost.
